  B.  Staffing  Approach

The City  of South Gate owns and operates  a municipal  groundwater  system  serving  approximately  14,300  service
connections.  Maintaining  continuous  regulatory  compliance  requires  qualified  certified  personnel  capable  of
supporting  daily  operations,  emergency  response,  capital  improvement  projects,  and specialized  regulatory
programs.  It is of utmost  importance  to maintain  an adequate  water utility  staff at all times,  all the way from  a
utilities  operator  and up into senior  management.  The times  are more critical  than ever as there is not only a
nationwide  but a global  shortage  of certified  water  experts  to go around.  This is why waterTALENT  is dedicated
to directly  address the growing  issue of sustaining  a proper  certified  workforce  by means of temporary  and
interim  relief.

As mentioned  in the previous  section,  waterTALENT  operators  aren't  exclusively  utilized  to just  fill  a role, but to
work  and collaborate  with  the existing  staff in making  forward  progress  in a multitude  of ways,  including  but not
limited  to: CIP upgrades,  project  management,  SOP/O&M  manual  review,  mentorship,  and of course  your normal
routine  day-to-day  operations.  waterTALENT  operators  can act as operators,  supervisors,  consultants,  or
directors,  with  each waterTALENT  operator  possessing  an average  of 20+ years of experience.  waterTALENT
vets and recruits  professionals  who care about the state of affairs  in this industry,  and therefore  don't  solely  exist
to "fill  a chair".

Every  waterTALENT  operator  undergoes  a rigorous  and structured  screening  process before joining  our network.
This includes  a personal  interview,  criminal  background  check,  motor  vehicle  record  review,  10-panel  drug
screening,  professional  reference  checks,  and certification  verification  through  official  licensing  authorities.  This
thorough  vetting  process  ensures we provide  utilities  with  qualified,  reliable,  and trusted  professionals.

The process  to procure  a temporary  waterTALENT  operator  is relatively  straightforward.

  1.  City  Identified  Need:  City  experiences  a job vacancy  they have decided  they would  like temporary
  support  for
  2.  Notice  to waterTALENT:  City  reaches  out to waterTALENT  identifying  the temporary  position  at hand
  (certifications  required,  specific  scope of work/job  description,  projected  start date etc.)
  3.  waterTALENT  Sourcing:  waterTALENT  takes provided  information  and sources  a candidate(s)  that fits
  the bill
  4.  City  Interview:  City  interviews  temporary  candidate  (by phone  or in-person  if convenient)
  5.  : (7 City wishes to proceed with candidate:) waterTALENT deploys candidate to the City
  6. Re-source:(7 City does not wish to proceed with candidate) waterTALENT identifies another candidate
  and repeats  step 3 until  right  candidate  is found

waterTALENT  is the premier  on-call  resource  for temporary,  licensed  water/wastewater  operators  where  they are
needed most. The above process  may be repeated  as many times  as needed  for as many vacancies  that require
temporary/interim  support.  waterTALENT  is seen as a vital  resource  for all of your planned  (and unplanned)  job
vacancies  and can be seen as your  dedicated  support  arm to fill  tliese critical  roles in as minimal  amount  of time
as possible.

Accessibility-wise  waterTALENT  is available  24/7 to field  calls for temporaiy  support,  including  for emergencies.

 ANALYSIS:  The  City  advertised  the  West  Side  Reservoirs  Rehabilitation  Project  for
construction  bids on August  3, 2026.  On August  27, 2026,  the City  Clerk  received  and publicly
opened  the following  three bids:

  Bidder  Name  Base Bid
  Capital  Industrial  Coating  $2,682,352
  J. Colon  Coating  -  $2,948,900
  Spiess Construction  Co.  $3,214,130

Staff  reviewed  the  lowest  bidder's  proposal,  licensing,  references,  and  qualifications  and
determined  that Capital  Industrial  Coating  is the lowest  responsive  and responsible  bidder  and
has the experience  and capability  to complete  the work.

Staff  therefore  recommends  awarding  the construction  contract  to Capital  Industrial  Coating  in
the amount  of $2,682,352.  Approval  will  allow  the City  to proceed  with  the reservoir  repairs  and
protective  coating  replacement  needed to preserve  the tanks and maintain  reliable  water  service.

BACKGROUND:  The  City  owns  and  operates  a  municipal  water  system  serving
approximately  90 percent  of South  Gate residents  and businesses.  The West  Side Reservoir  site,
located  at 2750 Tweedy  Boulevard,  includes  two groundwater  wells  and two  steel storage  tanks,
each with  a capacity  of 2.5 million  gallons.  Constructed  in 1999,  the tanks  are approximately  35
feet tall  and 94 feet in diameter.  Their  original  protective  coatings  consisted  of coal tar enamel
on the interior  and epoxy  on the exterior.  The exterior  roof coating  is now more than 25 years old
and has reached  the end of its service  life.

The West  Side Reservoirs  Rehabilitation  Project  is included  in the Fiscal  Year  2026/27  Capital
Improvement  Program.  The work  includes  preparing  and recoating  interior  and exterior  surfaces,
repairing  damaged  areas, and upgrading  railings  and ladders  to improve  safety  and maintain  the
tanks in reliable  operating  condition.

The  project  is categorically  exempt  from  the  California  Environmental  Quality  Act  (CEQA)
under  Title  14 of the California  Code of Regulations,  Section  15301,  Class  I(d),  which  applies  to
rehabilitation  of existing  facilities.

Construction  is anticipated  to begin  in November  2026 and be completed  within  ten months.

 Staff  negotiated  the proposed  fee from  $238,872  to $224,784  to align  services  with  project
needs,  The  revised  fee  includes  $154,784  for  construction  management  and  inspection  and
$70,000  for  geotechnical  and materials  testing,  labor  compliance,  monument  restoration  and
surveying,  and project  demonstration  support.

BACKGROUND:  The 5-Year  Capital  Improvement  Program  funds  annual  street improvements
through  the Residential  Resurfacing  Project  ("RRP")  to address road pavements.  A construction
contract  was  awarded  with  All  American  Asphalt  on  September  8, 2026.  Construction  is
scheduled  to begin  in October  of 2026  and be completed  in four  (4) months.  To ensure  project
success,  staff  recommends  awarding  Fountainhead  an agreement  for construction  management
and inspection  services.  These services  will  help the project  to ensure deliver  on time  and within
the budget.

On August  26, 2026,  the City  released  a Request  for Proposals  ("RFP")  for these professional
services  through  PlanetBids.  On September  14, 2026,  eight  proposals  were submitted  to the City
Clerk's  Office.  The  solicitation  established  a  qualifications-based  selection  process  that
considered  the qualifications  and experience  of the firm  and proposed  team,  project  approach,
understanding  of technical  and funding  requirements,  schedule  and staff  availability,  and the
proposed  level  of effort.

A three-member  technical  evaluation  panel,  comprising  the Division  Manager,  a Senior  Civil
Engineer,  and an Assistant  Engineer  from  the City  of South  Gate Public  Works  Department,  was

Ill. Project  Understanding  and Approach
We understand the City's project goals involve the Construction Management and Inspection services for the
Citywide Residential Resurfacing Project, Phase V For several streets within South Gate. The project will include cold
milling, ARHM pavement, Citywide residential slurry seal, localized pavement dig outs, surface preparation, crack
sealing, and weed abatement, signing, striping, markings, and pavement markings and railroad-crossing markings,
traffic loops, and restoration of affected traffic speed hump, new speed hump, adjustment of manholes, valves, and
utility appurtenances to Finished grade, and storm drain manhole, and such other items or details required by the
plans and specification. Milling is expected to remove 1 1/2 to 2 inches of material. The project is to be completed in
80 working days with a hard deadline for CDBG Funded work of November 16, 2026.

The Streets in Phase V include:

Firestone Boulevard  and Dearbom Avenue - Drainage improvements  including  full-depth  pavement
reconstruction,  curb and gutter, curb drains, parkway drain, curb-opening  catch basin, 18-inch PVC pipe,
local depressions, and incidental restoration.

CDBG - funded grind-and-overlay  improvements  on Elizabeth
Avenue, Virginia, Madison Avenue, Cypress Avenue, South Gate
Avenue, and Minnesota Avenue.

Additional  Phase V grind-and-overlay  improvements  on Roosevelt
Avenue, Arizona Avenue, Wilson Avenue, Hoover Avenue,
Mountain ViewAvenue,  Lincoln Avenue, and Industrial  Avenue at
the limits identified,

If awarded, conversion of the designated existing tennis court
area at South Gate Park into eight pickleball courts, including
surface preparation  and repair, acrylic resurfacing  and color
coating, striping,  posts, nets, and interior chain-linkfencing,

We are present through all steps of the project from pre-construction,
construction, and post construction. Our philosophy is to be proactive
and to mitigate problems before they arise, such as monitoring the
contractors and knowing the plans, specifications, permits and agreements as early as possible, while also being
vigilant of site conditions and contractor operations.

change order cost and schedule impacts are based on independentcost estimates developedconcurrently with the
Contractor's request and include a record of negotiations.This may also include a schedule fragment analysis using
Primavera P6 to manage progress recovery associated with the requested change.

the Project/Construction Manager, allowing him to involve the stakeholder if necessaryand resolve any technical issues.

from these experts will allow for seamless integration with the City.

  PURPOSE: To approve the grant deed for the right-of-way dedication to the City of South Gate
  ("City") for street purposes, in coimection with the development at 9313 Rayo Avenue, at no
  cost to the City,

  RECOM[MENDED  ACTIONS:  The City Council  wili  consider:

  a. Accepting a Grant Deed from Fubar Properties LLC., to secure right-of-way for street
  purposes as a part of the development located at 9313 Rayo Avenue, at no cost to the
  City; and
  b. Authorizing the Mayor to execute the Grant Deed in a form acceptable to the City
  Attorney and requesting the City Clerk cause the same to be recorded with the Los
  Angeles County Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk.

  FISCAL IMPACT:  There is no fiscal impact. The Grant Deed dedicatiori will be made at no
  cost to the City. While the prope'rty being dedicated has monetary value, it will be deeded to the
  City at no cost.

  ANALYSIS:  The City has the legal authority to require developers to dedicate land for public
  streets as part of the entitlement and approval process for new projects, This authority is granted
  by South Gate Municipal Code Chapter 5.32, California Government Code Section 37354
  (which allows cities to acquire property for public use), and California Government Code
  Section 66475 (which permits land dedications for streets, utilities, and other public purposes as
  part of development approval).

  As part of tis process, the Department of Public Works ('4Department") established conditions
  of approval for the development at 9313 Rayo Avenue. One of these conditions required a right-
  of-way dedication at the 2 feet of land to accommodate the future widening of Rayo Avenue.
  This requirement aligns with the City's legal authority under the aforementioned laws, The
  improvements will be deferred to a future time,

  I

  360
 BACKGROUND:  The proposed  development  is on Rayo Avenue  between  Firestone  Boulevard
and Southern  Avenue.  The development  consists  of the installation  of a modular  office  trailer
and exterior  site improvements,  including  a new  parking  lot,  landscaping/hardscape,  and  a
perimeter  block wall.

Currently,  the existing  right-of-way  along the development  frontage  is 70 feet wide.  The General
Plan  Mobility  Element  classifies  Rayo  Avenue  as a two-lane  collector  street,  for  which  the
ultimate  street width  is 72 feet. The proposed  dedication  will  widen  the right-of-way  along  Rayo
Avenue  to 72 feet, bringing  the development  into  compliance  with  the Mobility  Element  of the
General  Plan.

Resolution  No.  6536,  adopted  on November  9, 1999,  authorizes  the Mayor  to accept  grant  deed
dedications  without  City  Council  approval.  Given  that the Resolution  was adopted  more  than 25
years  ago, and consistent  with  City  practices  since  then pursuant  to Government  Code  section
27281,  staff  recommends  that  the City  Council  formally  accept  the Grant  Deed  to ensure  the
dedication  is clearly  authorized  and documented

  SUBJECT:  PROt'OSKU  USE OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA  OFFICE  OF TRAFFIC
  SAFETY  (OTS)  2026-2027  SELECTIVE  TRAFFIC  ENFOR(JMENT  PROGRAM
  GRANT FUNDS (STEP)

  PURPOSE,: To approve the use of the STEP funds in the amount of $126,400  for overtime,
  equipment, and training expenses.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City Council  will consider:
  a.  Authorizingutilizationofthe2025-2026SelectiveTrafficEnforcementProgram("STEP")
  Grant Funds in the amount of $226,400 for overtime, equipment, and training  expenses;
  b,  Amending  the Fiscal Year 2026/27 Law Enforcement  Grants Fund  Budget by
  approptiating $110,787 for overtime salaries, $3,000 for equipment, $9,860 for software
  licensing and $2,753 for training expenses; and
  c,  AuthorizingtheChiefofPolicetoexecutetheSTEPGrantAgreementinaformacceptable
  to the City Attorney.

  FISCAL IMPACT:  There is no fiscal impactto the General Fund andno requirement for the City
  to match the grant funds. The total amount of funding that has been allocated to the City for FY
  2026/27 is $126,400.

  ANALYSIS:  The South Gate Police Department submitted a grant application to the State of
  California Office of Traffic Safety (OTS) for the STEP Grant in early 2026, In September 2026,
  the OTS awarded the South Gate Police Department $126,400 for overtime, equipment, and
  training expenses.

  BACKGROUND:  The OTS strives to provide funding assistance to agencies with the gteatest
  need. The grants are awarded on a competitive basis, and a comprehensive evaluation is part of
  the applicationreviewprocess.  OTS evaluates applications using several criteriaincluding, butnot
  limited to, the potential traffic safety impact of proposed activities, local collision statistics, and
  OTS rankings,  the seriousness of identified  problems,  performance  on previous  grants,
  proportionality  of funding requested with identified traffic safety problems, and the value of the
  funding requested for the proposed activities.

  369
 In early 2026, the South Gate Police  Department  submitted  a grant proposal  to OTS seeking  grant
:[unding  to impact  traffic  and record  reporting  related  issues  in the City.  The goal of the STEP
program  will  be to reduce  the number  of persons  killed  and injured  in traffic  collisions  because  of
alcohol  and other collision  factors.  Using  best practices,  the South Gate Police  Department  intends
to impact  these issues through  DUI  Checkpoints  and saturation  patrols,  warrant  service  operations,
surveillance  operations,  and educational  awareness  programs.  The STEP program  will  also focus

 1.  PROBLEMSTATEMENT

 Describe  the city, county, or jurisdiction  this grant will impact.
 Located in the heart of the Los Angeles Metropolitan  Area, the City of South Gate is a busy, urban
 community consisting of residential, commercial,  and industrial development  spread over 7.4 square miles.
 South Gate is a vibrant and diverse city that has a lot to offer. From its rich history and cultural heritage to its
 numerous parks, shopping centers, and restaurants.  One of the most notable aspects of South Gate is its
 rich history and cultural heritage. The city was founded in 1923 and has since grown to become a hub for
 arts, culture, and entertainment.  South Gate Park and Recreation Center is a city gem, which hosts various
 community events, festivals, and cultural celebrations  throughout the year. It currently ranks as the 73rd
 largest city in California and 1 7th largest in Los Angeles County with a population of 98,633. The City of
 South Gate is also boarded by two highly traveled freeways, Interstate 710, and Interstate 105. Each of
 these freeways has freeway on-ramps and off-ramps in or near the City of South Gate.

 South Gate is 20 miles north of the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach, 7 miles south of downtown Los
 Angeles, and 13 miles east of the Los Angeles International Airport, making it an ideal location for residents
 in the Los Angeles County area, and a main thoroughfare  for regional, national, and global transportation.

 We recognize several ongoing traffic trends occurring in South Gate. First, our population is growing which
 means there is more vehicle traffic traveling the roads of South Gate. With this increase, there arises a
 greater likelihood for crashes to occur. Second, we have a large and increasing homeless population that
 traverses our streets and roadways at all hours creating additional bicycle and pedestrian traffic. The City of
 South Gate is an urban city situated between several metropolitan  cities such as the cities of Los Angeles,
 Downey, Lynwood, Huntington Park, Cudahy, Bell Gardens, and Bell.

 South Gate provides police services for a population of over 98,000 people. There are sixteen elementary
 schools, three middle schools, five high schools, and one college campus within the City of South Gate.
 There are several businesses  in and around these residential communities  and schools. Many of these
 businesses are manufacturing  and retail-type businesses that are primarily open during the daytime. There
 are also businesses open during the evening hours which provide evening entertainment  including alcohol.
 These establishments  include several restaurant-style  bars with dance floors.

 Describe  the problem(s)  to be addressed,  supported  by current and relevant crash data. (most
 recent calendar  year data/stats).
 The City of South Gate, like many California cities, suffered financially due to the 2010 recession. This
 recession saw a staff reduction of sworn positions of nearly 100 officers to 71. During the last decade and a
 half, our city has diligently attempted to recoup those numbers. Compounded  with the Covid-19 pandemic,
 our staffing levels have at times reached critical levels. The South Gate Traffic Services Bureau was initially
 reduced from six sworn officers to two sworn officers. With the recent improvement  in staffing the South
 Gate Traffic Services Bureau's staffing has improved to four sworn officers and eight non sworn Community
 Service Officers. Efforts are being made to increase these numbers further and the South Gate Police
 Depafment  has committed to making traffic safety a top priority.

 Despite these improvements,  our traffic officers have been tasked with backfilling Patrol deployment
 shortages by working mandatory overtime and handling calls for service involving traffic crashes. This
 greatly reduced the time traffic officers have been available to address hazardous drivers, pedestrian,  and
 bicycle safety issues. Because of this the directed enforcement  available through the grant assists in
 impacting these poor and dangerous driving habits. The City of South Gate has an average of 6.75 fatal
 traffic crashes per year from 2021 to 2025 (high of 8 in 2021).

 From 2010 to 2025 the City of South Gate has had over 5890 injury traffic crashes and over 8648 injured
 victims. Accordin to 2021 0TS crash ranki  s Grou  C the C  of South Gate ranks #5 in fatal and inau

  crashes,  #6 in speed-related  traffic  crashes,  #3 in nighttime  injury  crashes,  and #2 in hit-and-run  injury
 crashes.

  In 2022-2025,  South Gate identified improper  turning, unsafe speed, and right-of-way  violations as the top
 three primary  crash factors. (mproper turning  accounted  for a total of 1, 'l 74 crashes,  while unsafe speed
 contributed  to 756 crashes.  Right-of-way  violations  were  responsible  for 573 crashes  during  the same
 period.  Additionally,  in 2025,  there  were  39 alcohol-involved  crashes,  resulting  in 35 injuries  and 2 fatalities.
 These  crash  factors  indicate  a significant  safety  concern  for the South  Gate  community,  as the high volume
 of crashes underscores  the need for effective interventions  to address these driving behaviors.  By targeting
 these issues, South Gate PD can work towards  reducing the number of crashes and enhancing  road safety
 for all residents and visitors.

 The Traffic  Services  Division  conducts  several  DU checkpoints  each year.  With these  always  being  in the
 evening,  lighting  is always  an issue.  Once  set up, the check  points  have to main areas  that required
 adequate lighting, the screening area and the secondary  area. In the screening  area, additional lighting is
 needed so the officers can see for things such as open containers  inside vehicle and to make the officers
 safe and more visible. In the secondary  screening  area DUI investigations  take place,  vehicles  are being
 impounded  and citations are issued. it is critical to have adequate  light in these areas.

 Define  the target  population  the  grant  intends  to serve  and  how  they  are affected  by the  problem(s).

 The South  Gate  Police  Department  will aggressively  address  behaviors  that cause  traffic  crashes,  speed,
 DUI, unsafe turning movements,  and distraction.  We seek to reduce pedestrian  and bicyclist actions  that put
 themselves  in harm's way and also endanger  the motoring public. We believe that a well-formulated  traffic
 enforcement  plan will address  every  angle  of behavior  will greatly  reduce  the number  of injury  crashes  we
 have.

Project  Description:

The project goals are to fund the costs associated with implementing  a body worn camera program. The South Gate
Police Department  is committed  to a partnership  with our business and residential  community  to provide the highest
level of service based on trust and transparency.  Recent nationwide  events involving  police use of force have
generated  calls for law enforcement  officers to wear body-worn  cameras  (BWCs). This video footage will serve as
another layer of transparency  and provide unparalleled  public accountability  by providing a more detailed and accurate
account of the events. In terms of evidence collection,  the cameras will provide an invaluable  record of statements,
physical evidence and the timeline of events during crimes in progress and other critical incidents. The capture and
recording of these critical incidents and police related encounters  will serve to further strengthen  our relationship with
the community through increased trust and confidence.

  a agreements), including many provisions previously codified in Title 42 of the u.s. Code.

reclassified to the new Title 34 or the u.s. Code is to be read as a reference to that statutory provision as reclassified
  Title 34. This rule of construction specifically includes references set out in award conditions, references set out in
material incorporated  by reference through award conditions, and references set out in other award requirements.

Property  Tax
Property  Tax is the City's  second-largest  General  Fund revenue  source.  The FY 2025-26
amended  budget  projected  property  tax revenues  at $18,601,976. Through  June 2026, property
tax receipts  came in at $19,276,814, which  is $674,838  higher  than projections.  The primary
driver  is Residual  (AB  xl  26) revenue  which  came in higher  than projections  by $494,098.

Sales Tax
Sales Tax is the City's  largest  General  Fund revenue  source.  The FY 2025-26  amended  budget
for sales tax was $27,940,511.  Through  Jiu'ie 2026,  sales tax revenues  came in at $28,222,794,
which  is $282,283  higher  than projections.  Based  on HdL's  mid-year  analysis,  the FY 2025-26
Sales Tax revenue  estimate  was amended  downward  by $1,688,875  from  the adopted  budget.
Actual  receipts  then exceeded  the amended  estimate,  with  Local  (Measure  P) and State Sales Tax
above projections  by $178,182  and $104,101,  respectively,  driven  primarily  by strong  fourth-
quarter  receipts.

Other  Taxes
The Other  Taxes  category  includes  Transient  Occupancy  Tax, Franchise  Tax, and Business
License  Tax revenue.  Revenues  in this category  were lower  than projections  by $831,834.  The
primary  driver  was Business  License  Tax, which  was $1.1 million  lower  than projections
because  of a one-time  change  in timing,  not a decline  in the tax base. Renewal  payments
received  before  June 30 for FY 2026-27  licenses  are now recorded  as FY 2026-27  revenue,  the
year the license  covers,  consistent  with  modified  accrual  accounting  standards.  The FY 2025-26
budget  was prepared  under  the prior  practice  of recording  these payments  when  received.

Licenses  & Permits
Licenses  & Permits  revenue  totaled  $1,902,269,  which  is $342,006  above the amended  budget  of
$1,560,263.  NDES  and Industrial  Waste  permit  revenue  came in higher  than projections.  The
total  also includes  a $133,222  SEACCA  reimbursement  recorded  at year-end.

Intergovernmental
Intergovernmental  revenue  totaled  $481,540 through  June 2026.  This category  includes  Grants,
POST  Reimbursement,  and Motor  Vehicle  In-Lieu  Excess  revenue.  The FY 2025-26
intergovernrnental  revenue  was lower  than projections  by $655,662.  The primary  driver  is lower
than expected  grant reimbursements  for the All-Youth  Workforce  Program  in the amount  of
$766,590.

fees, and other user-based  charges.  ADU  Inspections,  Park Rents & Concessions,  and Aquatics
exceeded  projections  by $72,231,  $58,968,  and $84,017  respectively.  Strong  participation  in City

The Other  Revenues  category  includes  Administrative  Allocations,  Miscellaneous

amended  budget  of $6,392,995.  Through  June 2026,  Other  Revenues  were $1,138,510 below
budget.  The primary  driver  was Settlements  and Insurance  Recoveries,  which  were $684,074
below  budget.

General  Fund  Expenditures
General  Fund expenditures  totaled  approximately  $76,982,881,  or 98.3%  of the amended  budget.
Community  Development  finished  $1,408,569 under budget,  primarily  from  personnel  vacancies
and  operational  savings,  Public  Works  finished  $380,218  under  budget  from  vacancies,  and
Human  Resources  finished  $97,848  under  budget  from  operational  savings.  As part of the normal
year-end  close,  the attached  resolution  realigns  $1,865,974  of General  Fund  appropriations  from
Community  Development,  Public  Works  and  Human  Resources  to the  City  Manager,  City
Attorney,  Administrative  Services,  and  Police  budgets  and  to  transfers  out,  so that  each
department's  appropriation  matches  its final  spending.  This is consistent  with  the City's  budgetary
control  at  the  department  level.  The  realignment  does  not  increase  total  General  Fund
appropriations,  and combined  General  Fund  expenditures  and transfers  out finished  $331,881
below  the amended  budget.

Transfers

Transfers  out were $4,405,388,  which  is $962,181 above the amended  budget  of $3,443,208. The
additional  transfers  covered  operating  deficits  in other funds,  including  $206,435 to Housing
Authority  Fund,  $1,429,130  to Street Light  & Landscaping  Fund,  and $2,382,295 to Insurance
Fund.  The attached  resolution  aligns  the transfers  out appropriation  with  these final  amounts.
